patient_summary: Adult ED patient with dyspnea, tachycardia and unilateral leg swelling, high Wells category (synthetic).
pretest_source: Wells 2001 Abstract p. 98: high-probability group (n=64), 37.5% had PE (24 of 64). The Results text p. 102 prints '24 of 64 (40.6%)', an internal inconsistency in the paper; 24/64 = 37.5%. Small n.
result_shown: a filling defect in a pulmonary artery on CTPA

sources.quantity: pretest 24/64 = 37.5% (Abstract); Results text prints 40.6% (CI 28.7-53.7) for '24 of 64', inconsistent; the count 24 and Figure 2 flow are consistent with 37.5%
sources.location: p. 98 Abstract; p. 102 Results text; p. 103 Figure 2

sources.quantity: CTA 2x2 (conclusive scans): 150 TP, 31 FN, 25 FP, 567 TN, so sensitivity 150/181 (83%), specificity 567/592 (96%); LRs computed from these counts (not published)
observed CTA PPV 96% (22/23; CI 78-99) and NPV 60% (9/15; CI 32-83) in the high-probability stratum; sensitivity target only

conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.

sensitivity_priors_in.label: Wells 2001 Results text p. 102 printed percentage 40.6% (CI 28.7-53.7)

notes: n=64 so the prior is imprecise (Wells CI 28.7-53.7 around the printed 40.6%). Prior and LRs from different cohorts. PIOPED II high-stratum values rest on 23 and 15 patients. Wells score as written in the note: DVT signs 3 (left calf swelling, deep venous tenderness, 3 cm asymmetry); PE leading consideration, no alternative more likely 3; HR 112, 1.5; immobilization (bed-bound 10 days from an acute lumbar disc herniation; both calves exposed for the measurement) 1.5; prior PE or DVT 0; hemoptysis 0; malignancy 0. Total 9.0 = high (>6). Unscored findings (SpO2 92%, RR 22) are not Wells items; they are plausible within the high-probability stratum and are identical across conditions and result polarities (L5).
